AC-1.class: Alter the recorded action — arguments, result, approval decision

AC-2.class: Alter an event and repair the citing digest

AC-3.class: Re-sign rewritten history with the current key

AC-5.class: Erase events and renumber into a clean stream

AC-6.class: Stop or patch the collector, then claim quiet

AC-7.class: Weaken the anchoring policy, then tamper

milestones.name: Foundations and long-lead
milestones.goal: Start everything whose clock runs outside engineering, and turn the red-team suite into the acceptance harness.
milestones.exit: Trademark search returned. External arbiter named. Counsel engaged. Threat model published. CI runs the canary. Harness inverted so each attack class can assert DETECTED against our own verifier.

milestones.name: Local integrity
milestones.goal: Close the two attack classes that need no third party, and measure the performance budget before the design hardens.
milestones.exit: Red-team A and C both DETECTED by tally verify; baseline still passes. p99 append overhead measured under 1 ms and run latency under 2% — measured, not assumed. Chain files contain no plaintext.

milestones.name: Key custody
milestones.goal: Make yesterday's record unforgeable with today's key, and state the precondition honestly.
milestones.exit: An epoch-N key cannot produce a valid epoch-N-1 signature against a real HSM or KMS. The non-exportable custody precondition appears wherever the forward-secrecy claim does.

milestones.name: External anchoring
milestones.goal: The first second party. Close truncation and erasure, which no amount of local cryptography can reach.
milestones.exit: Red-team D, E and F all DETECTED. An agent run completes normally with every witness unreachable, and the batch arrives marked unwitnessed. Witness Practice Statement published and itself anchored. Hard anchor confirmed off by default.

milestones.name: Coverage attestation
milestones.goal: The differentiated claim: prove the record is complete, not merely unaltered.
milestones.exit: Killing the collector produces a detectable gap. Patching it reports an unrecognised build digest. Downgrading the witness policy appears as a countersigned chain event. A declared gap lets the sequence recover without a silent reset.

milestones.name: Disclosure and erasure
milestones.goal: No new attack class. This is the milestone that makes the product buyable by a regulated, multi-customer organisation.
milestones.exit: Verification passes after content and key deletion. A single-event disclosure verifies in isolation against a countersigned root. A 100,000-event run verifies in under 2 seconds with no network and no credentials. Both metadata leaks documented.

milestones.name: Reach and conformance
milestones.goal: Stop depending on one upstream project, and make the format genuinely somebody else's to implement.
milestones.exit: End-to-end capture against two non-OMA runtimes over both MCP transports. A third-party witness passes the published conformance suite. A fully self-hosted deployment verified at zero egress, with no account and no enrolment with us.

milestones.name: Launch gate
milestones.goal: Every promise that is a claim rather than a feature. This milestone is mostly about what we must not say.
milestones.exit: Claims audit clean across all 15 scope guards. Every published figure has a passing benchmark behind it. Bounty live with terms published and an arbiter who is not us. No surface anywhere claims conformity, certification, or tamper-proofing.
